title: Flipback tethering lab — late-night unpin & microflip notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal lab notes for a small 'flipback' (microflip) where we tether traffic and unpin a model version manually if heat appears. Mostly a scratchpad for late-night ops and for pairing with Maya next run.

Context: staging -> small subset of prod (0.5% -> 3%) via tethered cohorts. Target release: flip-2026-02-25 (model v1.9.2 -> v1.10-q2). We expect 1.2x token cost but 0.85x latency in p50 on the fast path. The goal for this session: validate telemetry and warm caches while keeping per-tenant risk low.

Quick TL;DR play:
- Start small: 0.05% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 3% (30m min between bumps)
- Always keep an escape hatch: trafficctl set-weight flip-2026-02-25 0 && route-default back to v1.9.2
- If p95 latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate delta > +0.7% -> immediate hold and investigate

Checklist (operational):
[ ] Preflight: verify warmup completed (kv cache > 60% hit), model pinned in targeted pool
[ ] Canary cohort: pick 3 low-risk tenants (non-SLAs) and 2 internal clients for first window
[ ] Logs: streaming to infra/logs/flipback-2026-02-25, subscribe (maya, ol)
[ ] Alert hooks: set ephemeral alerts for 15m windows on p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-fallback events
[ ] Instrument: inject lightweight synthetic queries (length distributions: short, med, long)
[ ] Telemetry sanity: compare token-per-second, avg-kv-latency to baseline

Operational knobs and commands (cheat sheet):
- trafficctl set-weight <release> <pct>  # set cohort weight (internal)
- trafficctl inspect <cohort> --metrics     # quick snapshot
- rci rollback --release <release> --reason "rapid-unpin"  # persistent rollback action
- ssh jump-proxy -> tail -f /var/log/redwood/runtime/serve-*.log | grep flip-2026-02-25

Metrics to watch (live panels):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (text-gen path) — baseline: p95=320ms; trigger: >480ms
- 5xx rate (%) — baseline: 0.12%; trigger: >0.8% absolute
- client-side error rate (client-reported) — baseline ~0.05%; trigger: >0.5%
- model-fallback events — count of automatic downgrade events; any >3 in 10m is suspect
- kv cache hit ratio — want >60% after warmup; dips -> cold start issues
- tokens/sec and GPU utilization per-pool — ensure not pegged to 98% for >5m

Decision ladder (what to do if things go sideways):
1) Soft hold: do not increase weight, pause any scheduled bump, notify the oncall and product PD
2) Quick revert: trafficctl set-weight flip-2026-02-25 0; confirm consumer traffic is routed to v1.9.2; note timestamp
3) Investigate: collect last 30m of logs, model-variant metrics, and recent kernel selection traces (path: /tmp/flipback-traces)
4) Rollback PR if root cause is code/model (rci rollback or open a revert PR for infra changes)

Notes to self (observations):
- When I tried a manual microflip last month, warmup step 2 was skipped for one tenant and kv cache stayed under 20% -> led to p95 spike. Need explicit warmup verification.
- Consider adding a temporary canary header so downstream clients can mark requests for quick correlation (X-Flipback-Cohort: ol-2026-02-25)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should product accept a small client-facing banner for early-bird tenants explaining minor instability windows? (ask Priya)
- Can we make trafficctl do a dry-run that simulates latency impact using past 24h traces? (file a ticket)
- Add a 'pre-bump checklist' action in Console UI so engineers can't skip warmup step (low-effort UX improvement)

Post-run notes template (fill after the flip):
- bump windows and timestamps (0.05 -> 0.5 -> 1 -> 3):
- warmup kv hit% per cohort:
- top 3 anomalies (error types + stack traces):
- exec commands run + who (ol, maya):
- decisions taken and why:
- followups and owners (JIRA tickets):

Temporary mental model: tether = soft leash. If the leash slips (unexpected fallback, traffic surge), yank immediately. Better to under-validate and iterate than to blast 10% and scramble.

References and snippets:
- quick rollback example: rci rollback --release flip-2026-02-25 --reason "p95 breach" --notify team/platform
- trafficctl example: trafficctl set-weight flip-2026-02-25 1  # set to 1% for cohort alpha
- synthetic query set (short/med/long): s-query-short, s-query-med, s-query-long (see /infra/synth/flipback)

Signature: Olan R.  — night-ops friendly notes.

Last quick note: leave this doc pinned to my Drive sidebar while testing; delete when we migrate items to the Confluence postmortem page.
